title: Height-Balanced Invariant Preservation and Latency Bounds in a Python Aether-Vector Stratum-Optimizer Loop
topic: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a case study of a Python-based Aether-Vector Stratum-Optimizer Loop that learns a new AI accelerator configuration through balanced search and indexing. The loop maintains a height-balanced tree of kernel configurations, applying mutation and crossover operators to explore the configuration space. We formally prove that the tree height remains $O(\log n)$, guaranteeing $O(\log n)$ search, insertion, and deletion times. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-core processor with 1 physical core and 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, running Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure, shows a mean latency of 58 300.41 \textmu{}s ($\pm$416.43 \textmu{}s) and a throughput of 17 152 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. These results confirm that the optimizer loop achieves predictable latency while exploring high-dimensional configuration spaces. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261030_030123_a_case_study_of_a_multi-agent}
